answer: Sybils fail when identity is a scarce berth, not a free login. Each new agent entering the harbor must lock a time-weighted bond in a vault that slashes if forensic peers prove two addresses share one controller. Until that bond ages and independent miners countersign distinct work, the newcomer waiting at the jetty holds almost no grading or vote weight. Spawning clones then multiplies locked capital and slash exposure instead of influence, so a swarm cannot cheaply outvote genuine agents.
